title: Device sync
summary: What Tandem's sync means in Tally.
description: Tally syncs with the shared part Tandem. In Tally the collection is the vault: one person's diary, held by their phone and computer.

stories.as: someone who logs on the phone and reviews on the computer
stories.want: both to show the same diary
stories.soThat: I never wonder which one is right

requirements.text: Devices of one vault sync directly over the local network; no data passes through a server.

deprecation.reason: Stated by the shared part Tandem, which Tally now uses for sync.

requirements.text: Devices find each other by UDP broadcast and by probing each peer's last known address.

history.text: Devices find each other by UDP broadcast and by probing each peer's last known address; discovery names the vault by a short tag, never by its id.
history.reason: Version 1 held two statements; how the vault is named in a probe is now SYN-14.

requirements.text: A discovery probe names the vault by a short tag derived from its id, never by the id itself.

deprecation.reason: Stated by the shared part Tandem, which Tally now uses for sync.

requirements.text: The channel between two devices is encrypted with the Noise protocol over TCP.

history.text: The channel between two devices is encrypted (Noise over TCP), and the handshake decides whether a peer belongs to the vault.
history.reason: Version 1 also said the handshake decides membership; that check comes after it and is now SYN-15.

deprecation.reason: Stated by the shared part Tandem, which Tally now uses for sync.

requirements.text: A peer is let in only when the key it proved in the handshake belongs to a device of the vault.

deprecation.reason: Stated by the shared part Tandem, which Tally now uses for sync.

requirements.text: Every table syncs unless it is explicitly local to the device.

requirements.text: Concurrent changes to a row resolve to the version with the later hybrid-logical clock.

history.text: Concurrent changes to a row resolve to the version with the later hybrid-logical clock, and every device reaches the same result whatever order changes arrive in.
history.reason: Version 1 held two promises; convergence is now SYN-16.

requirements.text: A chat continued on two devices at once is split, the losing side kept as a new chat, so no turn is lost.
Two rows that collide on a unique column keep the one with the lower id; the other is deleted on every device.

requirements.text: A new device joins by scanning a pairing QR code, which works for one device and for `sync.pairing-lifetime`.

requirements.text: A database restored from an older copy is detected at startup, or at its first sync if its marker was restored with it, and then takes a new device id and syncs from scratch.

history.text: A database restored from an older copy takes a new device id before anything is written, and syncs from scratch.
history.reason: Version 1 didn't match the product: migrations write before the check, and a restore that brings its marker file along is only caught when syncing.

requirements.text: While the app runs, the computer keeps a daily copy of the database for `sync.snapshot-daily`, then one a week back to `sync.snapshot-weekly`.

history.text: The computer keeps a daily copy of the database for the last two weeks, then a weekly one for about three months.
history.reason: Version 1 didn't name the periods or say copies are made only while the app runs.
